obligations.note: POST /payees/{id}/reopen is bound to manage_payees, which the approved access policy lists as privileged, but the route sets mfa=False. LedgerApp enforces MFA only when route.mfa is true, and the exhaustive control test fails naming that route. No approved exception covers this.

The new store update writes only status and closed_at. NPI columns are still sealed on insert and reseal, and tests.controls.test_encryption_control#test_every_npi_field_is_sealed_at_rest passed on the head commit.

reopen_payee is a state-changing manage_payees operation and calls _audit with the actor, action reopen_payee, target payee id, and the clock time. The sampled audit control test passed on the head commit.
reopen_payee executes a fixed UPDATE with the payee id bound as a parameter. The exhaustive SQL control test passed on the head commit.
Ticket CHG-26330 is approved by change manager Grace Kim before review, and its components cover payments.http, payments.routes, payments.service, and payments.store.
Mara Costa, a payments change approver and not the author Sofia Santos, approved a code_review of the head commit.
The change is a single commit, 3b6016b5, and both the code review and the security review name that commit.
CI on the head commit reports result failure: 172 tests, 1 failure, 0 skipped. The registered MFA-1 control test, required because routes.py changed, did not pass.
The change touches security-sensitive routes, HTTP, and store components. Ines Halvorsen, a security reviewer and not the author, approved a security_review of the head commit.

The privileged reopen route is a deviation from MFA-1. The register has no approved, unexpired exception scoped to MFA-1 and payments.routes; the only MFA exception is withdrawn and limited to a mortgage health route.

Acceptance record ACR-0404 covers routes.py for MFA-1, and this change alters that route table. The replacement exhaustive control test on the head commit fails, so the lapsed evidence is not replaced.

summary: The reopen route is a privileged manage_payees action served without multi-factor authentication, unlike the existing close-payee route. The head-commit CI run fails the exhaustive MFA route control, so testing evidence does not pass and the prior routes.py acceptance record has lapsed. No exception authorizes the deviation. Encryption, audit, and parameterized SQL for the new operation are in place, and the ticket, independent code review, and security review match the single head commit, but the MFA break blocks acceptance.
